title: Ultrafast and reference-free sequence discovery in single-cell data.
data_url: https://malva.mdc-berlin.de (search server); tools at https://github.com/malva-bio/malva and https://github.com/malva-bio/malva_client

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py found no PMCID, no full text, no supplement, no accessions, no NCBI GEO/SRA/BioProject links and no Zenodo/Dryad hits. I read the malva_client GitHub README. Searching the index needs an API token, and getting one means logging in to malva.bio with ORCID (Profile > Generate API Token). Results come back from server-side search jobs (gene, sequence of 24+ nucleotides, or natural-language query). The client is licensed Clear BSD. The FAQ page timed out, and the GitHub API call for the malva repo returned non-JSON, so I recorded both as unavailable.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The ~74 million cells from thousands of experiments, the reference-free search for mutations, splice junctions and pathogens, and the cell-type prediction from sequence composition all come from the abstract or press coverage. The README says '>7,000 single-cell and spatial samples'. Search snippets say the Malva Tools code is free for academic non-profit use. I saw no downloadable data table.

a1_downloadable.note: No downloadable dataset. The index can only be queried through a server API that needs an ORCID login and an API token (seen in the malva_client README). The underlying raw reads are public single-cell experiments, which are raw sequencing data and multi-terabyte.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: This is a search engine and indexing tool, not a labelled table. Any target (cell type, disease) would have to be built from per-sample metadata returned by queries. Judged from the README and abstract, not from files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked. Per-cell k-mer (short subsequence) content sits server-side and is not exported as a feature table.

a5_enough_rows.note: Abstract claims ~74M cells, but I verified no row count.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Petabyte-scale source data per the abstract; index size not stated
a6_fits_laptop.note: Rebuilding the index locally means raw reads, which our policy forbids downloading. Queries through the API return small slices only.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Abstract says ~74M cells; README says '>7,000 samples'. These don't conflict, but neither could be checked against files.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not checked. Cell-type labels in such atlases usually come from expression-based annotation, which risks leakage when predicting cell type from sequence content.

backbone.name: scGPT or Geneformer (single-cell foundation models), not assessed
backbone.licence: Malva client Clear BSD; Malva Tools academic non-profit only (from search snippet); index needs an account

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not assessed: stopped at Part A.

honest_claim_h3: Not assessed: stopped at Part A. This is a tool paper with no labelled dataset to model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the short RNA subsequences found in each single cell to predict that cell's type, without aligning reads to a reference genome.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-cell counts of short RNA subsequences from the Malva index. Number of usable cells is unknown, because the index is only reachable through a logged-in search API.
plain_idea.predict: Cell-type labels from the original atlas studies. Those labels were mostly assigned by clustering gene expression, not by an independent measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Reference-free cell typing would help with species that lack a good genome. But the authors already show this in the paper, and the data can't be exported for independent modelling.

ml_idea: Reference-free cell-type classification from per-cell k-mer (short subsequence) profiles. Moot: the index is a gated server-side search engine rather than a downloadable labelled table, and the paper itself already demonstrates this task.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; stopped at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already failed: the malva_client README requires an ORCID login plus an API token, and no bulk export of a labelled table is offered.

verdict_reason: A1, A2 and A6 fail. Malva is a search platform (software plus a server-hosted index of ~74M cells), not a dataset. It needs an ORCID login and an API token, and it offers no downloadable labelled table. Rebuilding it would need petabyte-scale raw reads. No GEO, SRA, Zenodo or supplementary data is linked to the paper.
